newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:
* Zairian rebels pushed past the government's army and were heading toward the capital.
* The Croation government has been confiscating homes that once belonged to ethnic Serbs and allowing ethnic Croats to move in, according to relief workers and diplomats.
* The U.S. House of Representatives passed a bill giving public schools more money and flexibility to educate children with disabilities.
* A friend of accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh was portrayed by the defense lawyer as a liar who hoped to avoid a long prison sentence.
* Bronx Borough chief Fernando Ferrer dropped out of the Democratic race for mayor, endorsing Manhattan borough president Ruth Messinger.
* An interracial couple have been awarded $640,000 after a federal jury in Manhattan found that a co-op board had discriminated against them by denying their application to move into the building.
* Experiments on human subjects are seldom tracked as closely as experiments involving animals, raising concerns that scientific research is being left unchecked.
